title: SciPy Interpolation and Estimating Values Between Data Points
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of scipy interpolation and estimating values between data points.

understand.concept: Interpolation estimates values between known samples. scipy.interpolate offers one-dimensional linear and spline methods, shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation and regular-grid interpolation. Choose a method based on smoothness and shape constraints; extrapolation outside the sampled domain requires an explicit policy and can be unreliable.

explain.narrative: This lesson explores scipy interpolation and estimating values between data points through deterministic examples. Use the appropriate SciPy API, inspect its return structure and validate assumptions about file formats, interpolation domains or statistical hypotheses. Interpolation estimates values between known samples. scipy.interpolate offers one-dimensional linear and spline methods, shape-preserving PCHIP interpolation and regular-grid interpolation. Choose a method based on smoothness and shape constraints; extrapolation outside the sampled domain requires an explicit policy and can be unreliable.

examples.title: Linear interpolation
examples.code:
from scipy.interpolate import interp1d
f=interp1d([0,1,2],[0,10,20])
print(float(f(1.5)))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates linear interpolation. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Cubic spline interpolation
examples.code:
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
f=CubicSpline([0,1,2],[0,1,4])
print(round(float(f(1.5)),2))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates cubic spline interpolation. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.

examples.title: Shape-preserving PCHIP
examples.code:
from scipy.interpolate import PchipInterpolator
f=PchipInterpolator([0,1,2],[0,1,4])
print(round(float(f(1.5)),2))
examples.explanation: This deterministic example demonstrates shape-preserving pchip. Inspect the returned values and consider how the method's assumptions affect real datasets.
